title: Large personal MSX graphics, Amiga IFF and Acorn discovery
summary: Personally screen 138 candidate URLs and add 33 projects, with two implementation-based exclusions.
notes: Root assistant personally performed all research and main-branch publication without a worker, PR or new branch. Twenty searches covered Amiga image/audio formats, MSX sprites and native graphics ports, Acorn reconstruction, Commodore editors and 68K debugging. Each addition has inspected implementation. Original historical source, annotated recovery, C ports, bytecode-free native graphics patches and host asset tooling remain distinct. Source limits override README overclaims: partial CPU semantics, absent image modes, broken export notices and external reconstruction dependencies are explicit. No build or emulator test was run; upstream fidelity and timing results are qualified. Agent-named files and configuration alone do not establish AI contribution. Two thin/example-only candidates were excluded on implementation evidence. Large files retain immutable source links rather than unverified rewritten excerpts.

sources.reason: Native live-coding editor embeds SJASMPlus-derived assembly and a Pentagon 128 execution view, with network broadcast modes.
Analyzes TAP headers/checksums, extracts BASIC and CODE data with manifests, and creates or appends loader/code blocks.
Converts classic DiskObject icons and IFF-family graphics using palette input, with PNG/ICO/SVG exports and newer icon decoding paths.
MOD loader and tick-based replay engine provide effects, stereo separation, filtered playback and WAV rendering.
MOD parser/replayer implements channel/effect state, seeking snapshots and PCM output through Java audio.
Author-published original source for the scrolling editor distributed in COMPUTE! Gazette January 1988, including keyboard and IRQ-vector integration.
Browser font editor maintains 256-character sets with binary/PRG, BASIC and cbmasm-style export paths.
Web editor provides annotated BASIC workflows and dialect-aware token tables, with disk and VICE debugging integration in separate components.
Editor rewrites labels, long variables, constants and compound assignments into numbered Commodore BASIC text.
Educational command monitor implements memory display/modification, fill/move/search, register-status display and numeric helpers in 68000 assembly.
Educational interpreter and assembly parser provide stepping, register inspection and a native GUI for a bounded instruction subset.
Restores Computer Concepts DitherExtend 0.60 as annotated ObjAsm and a routine-by-routine C module, covering dithering, blending and color-conversion SWIs.
Native Wayland viewer decodes ILBM bitplanes, ByteRun1, HAM/EHB and deep-color modes with CAMG/aspect-aware display.
Library reads IFF chunks and compressed/uncompressed ILBM plane rows, with info and SDL2 demonstration programs.
Pure-Swift parser converts 1–8 plane indexed ILBM and ByteRun1 data into CoreGraphics images.
Mandelbrot/Julia explorer combines native fixed-point assembly, chunky-to-planar drawing, ARexx controls and ILBM export with an optional FPU build.
IFF FORM reader/writer with ILBM and 8SVX codecs registered through Java ImageIO and AudioSystem providers.
Shared ILBM decoder supports Finder previews/thumbnails and Spotlight metadata across indexed, HAM/EHB and selected deep-color formats.
Author preserves a 1994 Battleship game with RS-232 two-PC experiments, single-player logic, sprite editor and custom Amiga ILBM import.
ILBM parser and GIMP loader recognize standard layouts and selected renamed chunk identifiers used in games such as The Clue and Whales Voyage.
C API detects, inspects and decodes ILBM/PBM, classic/MagicWB, NewIcons and GlowIcons into RGBA with PNG and optional SDL output.
Qt editor manages tiles, screens, sprite sets and palettes for SCREEN2/SCREEN4-oriented graphics workflows.
Browser editor represents 16x16 pattern masks and per-line mode2 attributes, evaluates layers and exports sprite data.
PNG conversion and checker build MSX2-compatible sprite layers, palette and OR-color combinations for native VRAM.
Splits 8x8/16x16 images into MSX1 single-color sprite layers and emits assembly or binary in hardware quadrant order.
Tauri desktop tool edits SCREEN2 tiles/maps and sprite sets, constrains per-row colors and exports JSON, C and raw VRAM data.
Swing editor records paths on a 256x212 canvas and exports absolute or relative C coordinate tables.
Patch ports sprite presentation to SCREEN4/mode2 on MSX2, disables the old sprite-sharing scheme and preserves an MSX1 conditional path.
Native Fusion C editor manages a 16x16 pixel grid with live sprite preview and multi-sprite positioning.
Delphi utility converts a 256x16 sixteen-color GIF strip to sprite-mode2 pattern/color tables with BLOAD output.
Retains reconstructed original game logic while replacing display with V9990 tile planes, metasprites, smooth scrolling and recolored editable assets.
Library exposes V9938 mode2 sprite position/pattern/visibility/EarlyClock functions through MSX BIOS for ROM applications.
Tkinter Spriter/Screener/Bitmapper suite prepares V9938 sprite patterns, maps and bitmap data, with BASIC detokenization utility.

Inspected batch script delegates conversion to SoX, selecting 8SVX versus fixed-rate raw fallback via a FORM text search and preserving directory layout. Useful collection-specific automation, but no independent codec or substantial analysis implementation warrants another catalogue entry.

Inspected WLA-DX source is a tile/sprite demonstration ROM and hardware setup example. No reusable tool, recovered program or substantive independent game/engine established; retain as teaching reference rather than inflate the catalogue.
